name: AKU Tanzania goes all out on International Women's Day

content.title: AKU Tanzania goes all out on International Women's Day
content.summary: The celebrations included mentorship sessions in primary and secondary schools, a fitness session and a staff breakfast

media.caption: The celebrations included mentorship sessions in primary and secondary schools, a fitness session and a staff breakfast
media.alt: AKU Tanzania goes all out on International Women's Day

content.text: For the team at the Aga Khan University (AKU) in Tanzania the International Women's Day is not just a one-day affair. It is marked through a series of events and activities over four days hosted by the University. This year, faculty and staff of AKU  engaged students and the community to bring the event's theme, "Each for Equal" to life through targeted activities.
The celebrations kicked on March 5 with presentations on women's health; a book review and a fitness session for AKU staff and students.

The next day staff visited Muhimbili Primary School to give a talk on sexual abuse to Grade 7 and 8 students. They also later donated food and household items to women suffering from Obstetric Fistula at the Comprehensive Community Based Rehabilitation in Tanzania.

On March 7, students from Tambaza High School visited the AKU Tanzania campus, to interact with the staff, and engage in sports activities. Together with staff, they also made IWD-theme friendship bracelets.

"This year the communities we serve and our nation at large saw AKU Tanzania in action. The celebrations were colorful, relevant and well-attended by both men and women," said Prof Joe Lugalla, Associate Vice Provost, AKU Tanzania, "the events were valuable not just in terms of ideas but also actions. They showed how much we as a University value, encourage and practice gender equality in the workplace."

The activities culminated in a staff breakfast and half-day celebration on March 9. There were panel discussions on women's health and rights, and a skit by Tambaza High School students on the importance of men enabling women in their careers.

Chief Guest, Ms. Mary Rusimbi, a gender expert and founder of Tanzania Gender Networking Programme (TGNP) said, "I urge AKU as a leading research institution in Tanzania to partner with local institutions in doing research with a focus on improving women's rights. It is through meaningful research that all women will be able to realize their full potential and engage in transformation for empowerment, social justice and application of women's rights at grassroots community, district and national levels."
This is what AKU faculty and staff had to say about the celebrations:

"It gives me great satisfaction to see a dream turn into reality! The vision behind planning and executing the various IWD 2020 activities, unlike other years, was to make a difference. A difference in the lives of other women around us, a difference in those who are in need, a difference in how we may uplift each other, a difference in how we can spread love and positivity, a difference in shedding light on social ills within our societies, a difference in generational equality, and ultimately, a difference in how we raise awareness about this year's theme," said Lucy Rweyemamu, Senior Manager, Dean's Office and the lead organizer of this year's celebrations.

"AKU Tanzania's IWD 2020 celebrations portrayed a true picture of equality. Through this event, women had an opportunity to showcase their strengths: the strength to plan, organize and manage events, address challenges in the community, provide care, and inspire others; men and women, young and old," said Nipael Mrutu, AKU Tanzania faculty.
The IWD events were aimed at not only celebrating women but empowering them to succeed in all aspect of life.
